scope: Windows local MCP protocol and one actual Codex host integration trial

prior_attempts.outcome: One request completed; closing its Windows MCP client killed the shared descendant service, resetting the other request.
prior_attempts.cause: Installed MCP SDK uses a Windows Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE; the daemon initially inherited that client job.
prior_attempts.note: MemoryError lines in the appended service log were historical and do not diagnose these attempts.

prior_attempts.outcome: Provider returned Selected model is at capacity before any MCP call.
Host reported truncated output for the flawed case and substituted insufficient_information while explicitly disclosing that the observed verdicts were unavailable.

successful_procedure.service_start: Explicit CLI startup outside either MCP client's Windows cleanup job
successful_procedure.host_calls: Three separate sequential tool executions with compact output, retaining findings, model disagreements, capacity gaps and source references
successful_procedure.host_model_identifier: Not explicitly configured or emitted by CLI

measurements.memory_measurement_limit: Sampled sum of service and child-process RSS, excluding the AI host; shared pages may be counted more than once. This is not a universal RAM requirement.

limitations: These known protocol fixtures verify composite plugin behavior and host fidelity, not model-only accuracy or production safety.
The unmodified Laya model predicted supported for all nine fixture checks; explicit rules preserved contradictions and missing-information verdicts.
No real deployment benchmark or production capacity was validated.
The trained experimental head was not activated in the plugin.
